items.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I play lead sometimes with Bill’s band when I can be here now, and I’ve told Bill up front

ctx.x: Hey — I’ll have to try that someday.

But you know I play lead sometimes with Bill’s band when I can be here now, and I’ve told Bill up front, I wouldn’t try and, you don’t even try to play those things the way Marshall did. It’s a whole different style. He played “Warm Valley” and the thing we’re going to play tonight “Isfa —” It’s a thing written for Johnny Hodges [“Isfahan”]. But all those things that are synonymous with either Johnny Hodges or Marshall, there’s no point in anyone trying to do that. That’s not the way I feel them, and I mean I can…
Okay, one more little finger buster here.
